physics_goals.quote: The CUORE experiment searches for 0νββ of 130Te using a tonne-scale cryogenic calorimeter operated at milli-kelvin temperatures.
physics_goals.value: Search for neutrinoless double-beta decay of 130Te using a tonne-scale array of cryogenic bolometers

summary.plain: A huge array of super-cold tellurium crystals under an Italian mountain, listening for a faint click of heat that would signal a rare radioactive decay. CUORE has been steadily collecting data since 2019.
summary.technical: CUORE (Cryogenic Underground Observatory for Rare Events): tonne-scale array of 988 TeO2 bolometric crystals (19 towers) operated at ~10 mK in Hall A of LNGS. Began operating in 2017, steady data taking since 2019; the 2024 result set T1/2 0ν(130Te) > 3.5×10²⁵ yr (90% C.I.) with over 2 t·yr TeO2 exposure. Predecessor to CUPID, which will reuse its cryostat.

unique_capabilities.value: First bolometric 0νββ experiment to reach the tonne mass scale, using a single large millikelvin cryostat
